pois.name: Sunshine 60
pois.description: 240 m skyscraper (1978), Japan's tallest building for 7 years. The Sky Circus observation deck on floor 60 gives a 360° panorama of the Kanto plain — Mt Fuji and Yokohama Bay visible on clear winter days.

pois.name: Ikebukuro Station
pois.description: The second-busiest station in Japan — 2.5 million passengers daily across JR Yamanote, Saikyo, Shonan-Shinjuku lines, Tokyo Metro Marunouchi and Fukutoshin lines, and Seibu/Tobu private railways. 60+ exits connect a vast underground shopping city.

pois.name: Sunshine City
pois.description: A 60,000 sqm urban resort built on the former site of Sugamo Prison (1978). 4 interconnected buildings: the Sunshine 60 tower, a 4-floor aquarium, the ancient Rome-replica Alpa shopping mall, and the Bunka Kaikan theatre. Tokyo's original city-within-a-city.

pois.name: Otome Road
pois.description: Ikebukuro's answer to Akihabara — a street of shops catering specifically to female fans of manga, anime, and BL (boys' love) content. Shops like K-BOOKS and Animate Lady draw Tokyo's largest community of female otaku.

pois.name: Animate Ikebukuro
pois.description: 8-floor flagship of Japan's largest anime/manga retail chain — 50,000+ items across manga volumes, figures, cosplay materials, and doujinshi. Ikebukuro's otaku heartland, rivalling Akihabara in scale and breadth.
